title: ?accept= query param reflected verbatim as Content-Type on blob downloads
description: Owner downloads a locally stored blob via GET /jmap/download/a-self/<id>/<name>?accept=text/html. The handler reads the accept query param, applies a weak filter (len≤256, exactly one '/'), and sets it as the Content-Type response header verbatim. A peer can deliver an HTML or SVG blob; if the owner is tricked into clicking a crafted download URL (e.g. embedded in a message), the browser executes the content in the kithd origin. Combined with the missing upload validation (blob.rs:44 accepts any content_type including text/html), this is a complete stored-XSS path. Fix: for locally stored blobs, read content_type from DB (set at upload time) rather than from the URL accept parameter. Also reject script-executable MIME types at upload time.
